metadata.title: Type V DMFs for CDER-Led Combination Products Using Device Constituent Parts With Electronics or Software Guidance for Industry
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 43 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 44 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 45 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 46 not required. 47

As stated in 21 CFR 314.420(c), the DMF holder 67 must submit any change, addition, or deletion of information to the DMF and must notify each 68 person authorized to reference the information. Therefore, an amendment to a Type V DMF may 69 be used to submit information regarding modifications to the device constituent part. 70 Amendments provide a regulatory pathway for the DMF holder to report device modifications 71 and for FDA to review device modifications, including those that may not warrant postapproval 72 reporting by applicants whose applications incorporate the Type V DMF by reference. 9
candidates.context: 8 Cross-center collaboration and/or consultation is important for combination product review. Although CDER is the primary contact for combination products as described in this guidance, CDER consults with other centers as described in FDA’s Staff Manual Guide 4101, Inter-Center Consult Request Process , available at https://www.fda.gov/media/81927/download . A DMF is neither approved nor disapproved. Its technical content is typically reviewed in 75 connection with the review of an IND, NDA, ANDA, or BLA. A DMF is not a substitute for an 76 application (e.g., if the device is also to be marketed alone). 77

candidates.statement: This guidance addresses process and general content expectations for Type V DMFs for such 106 device constituent parts. It does not address FDA premarket review standards or expectations for 107 such constituent parts or the combination products that include them. This guidance is also not 108 intended to suggest that a Type V DMF should be submitted to CDER if the sponsor has rights of 109 reference to an MAF located in another center containing the same information. 110

candidates.statement: As specified in 21 CFR 314.420(a) and noted in the DMF guidance, if a prospective DMF holder 117 intends to submit a Type V DMF, he or she must first email a letter of intent to the DMF staff 118
The letter of intent should include the following information: 122
candidates.context: • Name, title, address, and contact information for the prospective DMF holder and a 124 contact for FDA correspondence. 125

candidates.statement: • Purpose and rationale for submitting the Type V DMF, which should explain why the 136 information is not being submitted in an IND, NDA, ANDA, or BLA or amendments and 137 supplements to these applications (e.g., intent to use the device constituent part with more 138 than one drug product, submission of confidential or proprietary information that is not 139 available to the applicant). 140
candidates.context: • Brief description of how the device constituent part in the DMF is used or how it 133 functions in the combination product, if known. 134 If there are any questions, or if additional information is necessary regarding the letter of intent 142 or proposed submission, FDA will contact the prospective DMF holder to discuss and resolve 143 these issues. candidates.statement: Before FDA can initiate the technical review of the Type V DMF information in support of an 194 application, the DMF holder should submit a letter of authorization (LOA) to the DMF. The 195 LOA, which can be included in the original or in a subsequent submission, permits FDA to 196 review the Type V DMF and permits authorized parties to incorporate the DMF information into 197 the application. See section V.B.4 for LOA content recommendations. 198
candidates.context: D. Technical Review Process 192 During the technical review process, the Type V DMF information will be reviewed in 200 conjunction with the authorized application for the combination product. If issues are identified 201 during this review, they will be conveyed to the DMF holder per current procedures for DMF 202 submissions. At the same time, FDA will notify any applicants who have referenced the Type V 203 DMF that additional information is needed. 15 The general subject of the issues will be identified, 204 but the details of the issues will only be disclosed to the DMF holder. 205

candidates.statement: When a DMF holder amends a DMF, he or she must notify each person (i.e., applicant) 207 authorized to reference the DMF (21 CFR 314.420). It is the responsibility of each applicant to 208 then determine whether a submission to an approved or pending application is necessary. An 209 amendment to the Type V DMF used to support an approved NDA, BLA, and ANDA will be 210 reviewed according to current FDA procedures. Generally, this review is triggered by an 211 applicant’s submission of an amendment, supplement, or annual report. 212

candidates.statement: A Type V DMF amendment may be submitted for changes to the device constituent part (e.g., 349 design or software changes), testing of the device constituent part, or testing of the combination 350 product for attributes related to the device constituent part. When a DMF holder amends a DMF, 351 he or she must also notify the applicants authorized to reference the DMF (21 CFR 314.420). 352

candidates.statement: To help determine the impact of any changes or new information provided in the Type V DMF 367 amendment, the cover letter should briefly describe the change, summarize the analysis and 368 evaluation of the change, and identify the device constituent parts and combination products 369 affected by the change, especially if the Type V DMF is referenced by multiple products. These 370 recommendations are in addition to those identified in the DMF guidance and in the cover letter 371 template for subsequent submissions on the DMF web page. The cover letter should also include 372 a confirmation statement that the DMF holder has notified affected applicants of the change to 373 the DMF and the dates of the notifications. 374

candidates.statement: The technical information should include the same type of information as described above for the 383 original Type V DMF submission, but should focus on the proposed changes for which the 384 amendment is being submitted. For changes submitted in the amendment, the technical 385 information should include a detailed description of the change, the rationale for the change, and 386 the testing information or supporting documentation for the change. 387
